result.question: Model Mimir Labs year by year (5 years): parse every capitalization opportunity in concert — revenue, investment rounds, and acquisition — and tabulate enterprise valuation / growth potential, runway, and time to founder becoming a millionaire (paper vs liquid).

report.question: Model Mimir Labs year by year (5 years): parse every capitalization opportunity in concert — revenue, investment rounds, and acquisition — and tabulate enterprise valuation / growth potential, runway, and time to founder becoming a millionaire (paper vs liquid).

prediction.headline: A small pre-seed (~$400K at $4M pre) closes around month 50; nothing larger is fundable on $65K ARR growing 6%, and no exit consummates inside the horizon.
prediction.likely_lead: Ironspring Ventures or Ben Franklin Technology Partners (C&N PA) — the only two capital personas that stay 'engaged' with stage-sized indicative checks ($250K / $150K)
prediction.terms_estimate: Pre-seed, ~$400K proceeds on a $4M pre / $4.4M post, ~9.1% dilution; SAFE or priced note. Seed and Series A remain fiction at this ARR/growth.

founder_millionaire.note: PAPER millionaire crosses in Year 5, and the source is the priced round, not revenue: 90.91% ownership x $4.4M post-money = $4.0M paper. Revenue alone never gets there — at 6x, $66.8K ARR marks only ~$401K, far under $1M. LIQUID stays null all five years: founder never draws salary (ARR peaks at $66.8K, far below the $255K = 3x-base draw trigger), takes no secondary, and no acquisition closes. The standing $650K NTT/EPAM offer is a marking signal, not a consummated cash exit, and even at a 70% cash portion x 90.91% would yield only ~$414K liquid — below the millionaire line. Liquid millionaire is out of reach within the horizon.

financial_outlook.one_liner: Real but tiny SaaS — $66.8K ARR at ~89% gross margin after five years — that becomes a Year-5 PAPER millionaire purely via a $4.4M-post pre-seed mark, while LIQUID net worth stays at zero because the founder never draws and never exits.

growth_potential.value_creation_story: Marked valuation climbs in two distinct regimes. Years 1-4 it is purely revenue-driven (ARR x6): $94K -> $151K -> $366K -> $388K, tracking the ARR build from $15.6K to $64.6K — strong YoY ARR growth early (61%, then 142% in Year 3 as subscriptions and services stack) that then flattens hard to 6% in Year 4 and 3% in Year 5 as the solo-founder capacity ceiling bites. Then in Year 5 the valuation source switches from 'revenue' to 'round': the $4.4M pre-seed post-money replaces the ~$401K revenue mark as the max(), causing the headline valuation to jump ~11x in a single year. That single repricing event is why valuation CAGR (161.8%) wildly outruns ARR CAGR (43.8%) — the growth is financing-driven, not earned by recurring revenue. The standing $650K acquisition offer never becomes the marking max because the round post-money exceeds it. The honest read: enterprise value is real but small and capacity-bound; the eye-catching ending number is a negotiated round mark on a still-tiny revenue base, not a revenue-substantiated valuation.

report.causal_narrative: Years 1-2 are the underwater wedge phase: the founder lands paid Ratatosk diagnostics for first revenue ($15.6K then $25.2K ARR) at 83% gross margin, but $44.8K fixed OpEx and zero outside cash drive cash to -$51K — the company survives only because lifestyle is externally funded and no salary is drawn. Year 3 is the operational high-water mark: a Yggdrasil subscription plus services push ARR up 142% to $61K, gross margin rises to 90%, and the company turns its first (thin) operating profit, lifting the revenue-based mark to $366K. But the binding constraint — one AI-augmented founder — then caps growth: ARR adds only 6% (Year 4) and 3% (Year 5), production deploys stay at one tenant, SOC 2 never completes, and the open data-loss blocker keeps regulated prospects parked, so the seed and Series A 'arr_floors' ($600K / $2.5M) are never cleared. The one financing event that does fire is a ~$400K pre-seed at month 50 ($4.4M post), which dilutes the founder to 90.91%, injects the cash that lifts ending balance to $331K (then Year-5 OpEx triples to $136K on the post-raise hire/spend, turning net negative again), and — decisively — re-marks the company at $4.4M, making the founder a Year-5 PAPER millionaire. Across all three tracks the verdict is consistent: revenue creates a real but small, capacity-bound asset; investment supplies the only millionaire-making mark but only at micro-round scale; and acquisition stays optionality (a $650K standing NTT/EPAM signal) that never closes, leaving LIQUID net worth at $0 throughout.
caveats: LIQUID never crosses $1M and is in fact $0 every year: the founder draws no salary (ARR never reaches the $255K = 3x-base trigger), takes no secondary, and no exit consummates — so the 'millionaire' status is paper-only and illiquid.

The Year-5 valuation jump to $4.4M is a financing artifact (round post-money), not revenue-substantiated; at the 6x ARR multiple the business marks only ~$401K. Valuation CAGR of 161.8% massively overstates underlying business growth (ARR CAGR 43.8%).

Round close is modeled as occurring at month 50 with ~9.1% dilution; the persona table shows most capital sources skeptical/cold and explicitly call the $40M-pre Series A 'fiction,' so even the small pre-seed close carries real execution risk (distribution: 55% closes / 30% partial-or-bridge / 15% stalls).

Growth stalls structurally at 6% then 3% YoY because of the solo-founder capacity ceiling, open critical blockers (YGGDATA-258 data loss), and incomplete SOC 2 — these gate the enterprise/regulated cohort and keep ARR two orders of magnitude below the seed/Series-A floors.

The $650K NTT/EPAM offer is a standing marking signal, not a binding term sheet; even if consummated at the 70% cash portion it would net the founder only ~$414K liquid, below the millionaire threshold.

Year-1 and Year-2 cash is negative (down to -$51K); the model only stays solvent because founder lifestyle is externally funded and no draw is taken — a genuine bridge or services-cash gap could break the timeline before the pre-seed wire lands.

swing_factors.factor: Breaking the solo-founder capacity ceiling (post-raise engineering hire actually shipping)
swing_factors.why: ARR stalled at 6% then 3% is the root cause that keeps the company below every round floor and at a small acqui-hire valuation; added throughput is the only path to seed-stage ARR and a revenue-led (not financing-led) valuation.
The open data-loss blocker (YGGDATA-258) and missing certs keep the regulated/defense cohort and enterprise references parked, capping deal size and gating the Series A thesis.

swing_factors.factor: Whether the pre-seed wire actually lands at month 50
swing_factors.why: It is the single event that makes the founder a paper millionaire and lifts cash to positive; with most capital cold, a stall (15%) or bridge (30%) would erase the Year-5 mark and leave valuation at the ~$401K revenue level.

swing_factors.factor: Consummating the NTT/EPAM acquisition vs. leaving it standing
swing_factors.why: It is the only realistic LIQUID path in-horizon, but at $650K x 70% cash x 90.91% it nets ~$414K — below $1M — so even a close does not make the founder a liquid millionaire; a materially higher strategic bid would be required.
Until ARR hits 3x base, the founder draws $0 and the slow salary-minus-lifestyle liquid path contributes nothing; ARR peaks at $66.8K, so this trigger is never hit and liquid net worth stays at $0.

paper.basis: ownership × marked valuation, where valuation = max(ARR×multiple, round post-money, standing acquisition offer). ILLIQUID.

liquid.basis: acquisition cash-out + founder secondary + slow (salary − lifestyle) accrual once drawing (ARR ≥ $255K). Lifestyle externally funded until draw. A fundraise yields $0 liquid.
